clips.text: What. No, wait. The station line. So you are the new one. You have four minutes. I have a soldering iron in my hand and I am not putting it down for you.
What is on the card! It is printed! Somebody typed it so that I would not have to say it to you on the telephone!
Point, tune, record, register, file. Amber is normal. If the amber changes you write it down. You do not have a feeling about it. Nobody has ever fixed a receiver with a feeling.
Half! You went and counted, or you are guessing? No. Do not tell me. Count them. Then the outer branches, in the order on the sheet, not in the order you like.
And when you finish you put my tools back where they were. Himmel. Where they were. I will know.
No.
I said no. Is this the service line? Then you ask me about service.
It is a list! I sent somebody to look for a pump in somebody's fence! That is what that was. A pump.
Then you leave them wired where they are. They are good tags. Dated, initialed, one to a stop. Do you know how rare that is, in this county? Do you?
Leave them.
Alone. In that truck, with those brakes, and at what hour? Verdammt. Did you touch it?
Then you have learned nothing, and it cost you a tank of gas. Stay off that flat. I do not need another form to fill in.
Every night. About the coffee. About a lamp. Reyes would read me the same number twice because it was funny, and it was not funny.
There is a message on my machine. I have played it one time.
It said what it said. You are not going to hear it. Go and point your antennas.
You wrote down when it starts? When it stops? Then you have two numbers, which is two more than you had. Nein. I do not want to hear what you think it was.
Sleep in the building tonight. Door shut. That is not an order. Nobody here can give you an order, apparently.
Because the telephone rings! What kind of question is that? Somebody at that station calls, at night, and somebody picks up. That is how it is supposed to work.
Have you eaten? There are crackers in the bottom drawer. Still in the wrapper. You did not hear it from me.
So hang them! Go! Everybody goes! I have worked with people who could not find their own feet with both hands and they all had somewhere better to be!
Not on hook one. Any other hook. Hook one you leave.
You call the service line about paper? I sign for parts. Ward signs for paper. Ask Ward.
Then the answer is the same, only louder. Not in my drawer. Not on my bench. Ask Ward.
Dale, field maintenance. You are the new one. Amber is NORMAL. Do not touch Bank Three. I do not care who you are. Dale out.
One job filed. I will alert the newspapers. Now the next one.
Who told you to go in that locker? Nobody. That is who. Leave the mug where it is.
You are out on my survey now? Nobody asked you. You read the tags, you do not add to them. Dale out.
It is after two. Are you in the building? Do not tell me about the sky. Be in the building.
You mended a branch. I looked at the line from here. It is a clean joint. Genau. That is the first thing anyone has done right out there since April. Do not get used to me saying it.
Ten jobs. Ward told me, I did not ask her to. It is almost competent. Keep going.
Your log has a hole in it. You put a time on each end of it, in ink, and then you call me. Not before, Mensch.
Twice now. Ward told me. One more and they give your nights to somebody else. After dark you stay in the building. Verstanden?
Three days to Ward's assessment. She reads numbers. I have seen your numbers. Stop looking out the window and file something.
The deputy called my bench. Somebody has been out at wagon 23, he says, and he has an idea who. Leave that one to the county.
Somebody saw you out at the mine on the west side. That is as far as you go. Not in. Not for a list, not for anybody. Dale out.
You are still on nights. They had a pool on you at the district. I said three days. Now I owe a man in Socorro five dollars.
So she kept us. I ran the whole array up and down from my bench, to see if it still moves. It moves. Do not get used to it. Dale out.
Your chart has a burst on it at ten to one. Ten to one! Who keeps appointments in this county? You run the control, then you file. Not the other way.
You are asking around Caliche after somebody who is not at their post? The county rang my bench. You are the station, not the county. Write what you saw.
You walked out on their raked ground? Do not tell me. Write down how wide the circle was and the time, and do not go back. Verstanden?
Somebody in Caliche is not at their post, the county says. People go to Belen. People come back. You do your card, and you lock the door. Dale out.
The deputy drove past wagon 23. Somebody has been in it since April, he says, and wiped the dash. Not him, not the district. You stay off that flat. Dale out.
A week to Ward's numbers. I have shut the pool at the district: nobody would take the other side of it. Do not make me open it again. Dale out.
Their van is out there with the door open, the deputy says. You do not go and close it. You write down where, and you stay in the building.
Helicopter low over the land this morning, and two cars that are not the county's. You did not see them. No. You write down that you did, with the time.
The attendant says you have the thermos from unit 23. Tag it and put it in the outgoing tray; the district runs it to Socorro. Do not drink from it, Mensch.
You were out at wagon 23 again, reading the dash? The deputy read it in April. He wrote down the number and not one word of what he thought. Do the same.
The county inspector wrote to you? He wrote to my bench too. He wants to know whether the array moves. I said ask the operator. So make it move.
You let the people with the van into my station? They read my logbooks. I know, because the logbooks are in order now, and they never are.
You filed an assessment. Now the county reads it and rings my bench to ask what it means, and I say ask the operator. Do not make me a liar.
Two weeks, and half my array is still lying on its back. Ward reads that line first, the county second, and I read it every morning. Mend something.
SARO night, this is Dale. Come in.
Night operator! I know you have the set. Come in!
Nothing? Fine. Then it goes on a slip by the phone. Dale out.
Finally. Next time you answer the first time.
Again? What. Nothing? Then take your thumb off the button. Dale out.
That is four times today. Four! I am turning my set to the wall. Call the service line in the morning. Dale out.
Now you call! I called you before, on channel one. You keep it on one, and when I call, you answer. Dale out.
You are driving and talking on my channel? Both hands on the wheel. Out.
You sound wrong. Both times are in the log? Good. Tonight you stay in the building. Dale out.
At this hour? You are inside? Good. Stay in. You do not open the door to look at anything. Dale out.
After two and you are outside? Nein. I do not want to know why. Go in. Now. Dale out.
Do you know what time it is? I know what time it is. Is something on fire? No? Then write it in the log. Dale out.
I am up a pole in the sun with a meter in my teeth. Call the service line like a person. Dale out.
You are standing next to a telephone. A telephone! Use the card, use the telephone, and leave my channel alone.
Antennas down, and you call me? The sheet has the order. Read the sheet, then mend them. Dale out.
Where are you, out there with my truck? You bring it back with four tires and gas in it. Dale out.
What. Is it the amber lamps? The amber is normal. Do the card. Dale out.
The county put a call through to my bench, so now it is your problem.
I am not driving out there. Dale out.
Leave the array where it is until I have read the encoders myself. And if you go out there, you go by daylight, and you take the walkie. Out.
SARO, Dale. Pick up.
SARO! The walkie. Now.
Fine. I leave it on the slip by the phone.
